name: The Enochian System of John Dee
dom: angelic revelation; the divine (Enochian) language; theurgic cosmology
note: The integrated angelic-magical system received by John Dee and Edward Kelley 1581-1587 across the Heptarchia Mystica, Liber Loagaeth, and Liber Scientiae (the Aethyrs and Great Table); its component structures are well documented even where individual angel names vary between manuscripts.

name: Carmara
dom: chief governance of the Heptarchic kings; presidency of the heptarchic order
note: The overarching/chief king coordinating the seven in the Heptarchia; Dee's records suggest Carmara and Baligon may be two names/aspects of the same governing king (flagged as a manuscript ambiguity).

name: Baligon
dom: government of the air; closely identified with Carmara's office
note: A Heptarchic king frequently equated with Carmara in Dee's diaries; the relationship between the names Baligon and Carmara is genuinely ambiguous in the records.

name: Bobogel
dom: government of his day; commonly associated with wisdom/Mercury
note: One of the seven Heptarchic kings; the Wednesday/Mercury correspondence follows the common reading, but planetary-day assignments vary between reconstructions of Dee's tables.

name: Babalel
dom: government of his day; the waters and martial force (Mars)
note: One of the seven Heptarchic kings, linked to Mars and to dominion over the seas in Dee's notes; precise planetary-day mapping is subject to manuscript variation.

name: Bnaspol
dom: government of his day; the earth and its riches (Saturn)
note: One of the seven Heptarchic kings, linked to dominion over the earth; the Saturn correspondence follows the standard reading but day/planet assignments are not uniformly fixed.

name: Bynepor
dom: government of his day; life and the estate of nature (Jupiter)
note: One of the seven Heptarchic kings, associated with life and the universal preservation of nature; the Jupiter correspondence is the common reading and varies between reconstructions.

name: Bnapsen
dom: government of his day; countering evil spirits
note: One of the seven Heptarchic kings; its day/planet assignment (often given as Friday) is among the least stable in the records and is flagged as uncertain.

name: Hagonel
dom: princely ministry serving the chief king; mediation of his authority
note: The prince attached to the chief king (Carmara/Baligon) and the most prominent of the seven princes in Dee's diaries.

name: Bornogo
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes in Dee's tables; the exact spelling and the king served vary between manuscript readings (flagged uncertain).

name: Befafes
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king; associated in some readings with the waters
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes; pairing to a specific king and spelling vary across Dee's tables (flagged uncertain).

name: Butmono
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes; the spelling and king served are subject to manuscript variation (flagged uncertain).

name: Blisdon
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes; spelling and king-assignment vary across readings of Dee's tables (flagged uncertain).

name: Bralges
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes; the spelling and king served vary in the manuscripts (flagged uncertain).

name: Bagenol
dom: princely ministry serving his governing king
note: Listed among the seven Heptarchic princes; spelling and king-pairing are uncertain across Dee's tables (flagged uncertain).

name: The Four Enochian Watchtowers (Great Table)
dom: elemental governance of the four quarters (Air/East, Water/West, Earth/North, Fire/South)
note: The four great elemental tablets of the Great Table received by Dee and Kelley, each governing one element and quarter; the individual square-angels and elemental Great Kings are deliberately not enumerated to avoid invention.

name: The Thirty Aethyrs (Aires) of the Enochian System
dom: thirty graded spiritual spheres enclosing creation, from lowest to highest heaven
note: Thirty concentric Aethyrs recorded in Liber Scientiae, ascending from TEX (the 30th, lowest) to LIL (the 1st, highest); only the firmly attested example aethyrs are listed individually.

name: LIL
dom: the first and highest Aethyr, nearest the divine
note: Named in Liber Scientiae as the first (highest) of the thirty Aethyrs; firmly attested in Dee's records.

name: TEX
dom: the thirtieth and lowest Aethyr, nearest the material world
note: Named in Liber Scientiae as the thirtieth (lowest) of the thirty Aethyrs; firmly attested in Dee's records.
